content.text:
Results so far:
- Top-level `es-toolkit` `words` differs from lodash on 129 of 200k domain strings (digit/uppercase boundaries), so it is not usable as-is.
- Compat `words` matched lodash on all 200k strings.
- Compat `isEmpty` matched on all 100k values, and `groupBy` (keyed on `age`) matched on all 20k row sets.

Next I'll check the compat `groupBy` signature (it might accept `'age'` directly, avoiding an adapter) and measure the baseline bundle size.

content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, and across about 200k sampled inputs its results match the original exactly.

**Size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 1526 bytes (min+gzip) and 98 bytes of own code. The original `src/module.ts` reports 9874 bytes and 169 bytes.

**What each function uses:**
- **`tokens`** uses `es-toolkit/compat/words`. The top-level `es-toolkit` `words` splits some inputs differently from lodash. For example, `"ab12cd"`-style digit/letter boundaries and `"HTTPRequest2x"` come out differently, and 129 of 200k domain strings mismatched. The compat version matched lodash on all of them.
- **`byAge`** uses the top-level `es-toolkit` `groupBy` with `row => String(row.age)`. This is the one adapter, needed because the call shape differs from lodash's `'age'` property shorthand. The compat `groupBy` also accepts `'age'`, but it bundles to 3996 bytes, so I didn't use it.
- **`isBlank`** uses `es-toolkit/compat/isEmpty`, which matched lodash on all 100k sampled values.

**Things to know:**
- `src/module.ts` is unchanged, so the lodash imports are still there. I only wrote the new file to `out/module.ts`, as asked.
- `package.json` has no dependencies listed, and `es-toolkit` is only present in `node_modules`. If this ships, `es-toolkit` needs to be added to `dependencies`. I didn't install or edit anything.
- The `es-toolkit` compat imports are default imports from flat paths (`es-toolkit/compat/words`, not `…/compat/string/words`).
